content: Beta-ureidopropionase is an enzyme encoded by the UPB1 gene in humans. The protein produced by this gene is a member of the CN hydrolase family. Beta-ureidopropionase plays a critical role in the pyrimidine degradation pathway by catalyzing the final step of this process. Specifically, the pyrimidine bases uracil and thymine are broken down through a sequential enzymatic process involving dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DHPDH), dihydropyrimidinase (DHP), and beta-ureidopropionase (UP). This degradation ultimately results in the production of beta-alanine and beta-aminoisobutyric acid. Deficiencies in beta-ureidopropionase activity are associated with a condition known as N-carbamyl-beta-amino aciduria. This metabolic disorder can lead to disruptions in neurological function and activity.
